title: VIJAY KUMAR versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 60 of 2025
22 September, 2026
Vijay Kumar --Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
with
Writ Petition Service Single No. 2407 of 2024
Vijay Kumar --Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, learned Counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand-respondents.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
The petitioner, pursuant to an advertisement
issued by the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service
Selection Commission ("UKSSSC") dated 24.08.2021,
submitted his application for appointment to the post of
Driver in Government Department of State of
Uttarakhand.
2. The petitioner participated in the selection
process and he was duly selected after the driving test.
The UKSSSC recommended the name of the petitioner
to the forest department for appointment as a driver,
subject to document verification conducted by the
department. The respondent no.4, vide order dated
23.08.2024, called upon the petitioner to appear on
30.08.2024 at 11:00 a.m. along with the original
educational testimonial, driving license, Caste
certificate, Certificate of selection category, Permanent
1

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
Resident certificate and other certificates with
photocopy of all the certificates duly attested by a
Gazetted Officer. The petitioner appeared before the
respondent No.4 along with the aforesaid documents
and the documents of the petitioner were verified. Still,
the petitioner was denied appointment. Rather nine
other candidates, who appeared for their document
verification, were given appointment.
3. When the petitioner was not issued any
appointment letter, pursuant to his selection and
document verification, he moved a representation to the
respondent No.4 on 10.10.2024 asking for the
appointment and to explain as to why the petitioner has
not been given appointment as given to nine other
persons, who appeared before the respondent No.4 with
petitioner for document verification. When no decision
was taken on the representation submitted by the
petitioner, petitioner moved the High Court by filing
Writ Petition No. 2407 of 2024, Vijay Kumar versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others.
4. In the said writ petition, on 06.01.2025, the
Coordinate Bench of this Court had kept one post of
driver vacant till the next date of listing. During the
pendency of the aforesaid writ petition, the
representation dated 10.10.2024, submitted by the
petitioner, has been rejected by respondent no.2 vide
order dated 03.01.2025 and the petitioner was found
unfit for the post of driver as according to the
respondent no.2, during the character verification, the
police department and the LIU have given negative
report against the petitioner. In the LIU report and the
2

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
police report, it was found that two criminal cases were
pending against the petitioner, which are as follows:-
 (i) FIR No. 0055 of 2023 dated 02.03.2023 under Section
379, Police Station Chapaar, District Muzaffarnagar
(Uttar Pradesh).
 (ii) FIR No. 0316 of 2023, dated 09.12.2023 under
Section 323, 504 and 506 registered at Police Station
Nangal, District Saharanpur (Uttar Pradesh).
5. It appears that due to the pendency of these
two cases, the petitioner was denied appointment as
driver with the respondent department.
6. Feeling aggrieved by the order dated
03.01.2025 passed by respondent No.2, the petitioner
has moved this Court by filing the present writ petition
WPSS No.60 of 2025, "Vijay Kumar versus State of
Uttarakhand and Others". Both the writ petitions are
being decided by the common judgment.
7. It is contended by learned counsel for the
petitioner that the advertisement was issued on
24.08.2021 by the UKSSSC and the petitioner
submitted his application on 11.09.2021, much before
the registration of the aforesaid two FIRs lodged against
him.
8. It is contended by learned counsel for the
petitioner that since at the time of submission of the
application form, there was no criminal case registered
or pending against the petitioner, he has not
suppressed any information to the respondent-selecting
body or to the respondent-department.
9. The FIRs were registered subsequently first
on 02.03.2023 under Section 379 and 411 of IPC and
3

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
the second on 09.12.2023 under Section 323, 504 and
506 IPC. Thus, there was no case of suppression of
facts made against the petitioner.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner further
submits that at the time of document verification, no
such information was asked from the petitioner.
Therefore, there was no occasion for the petitioner to
disclose the pendency of the aforesaid two FIRs lodged
against him.
11. Learned counsel for the petitioner also
submits that in one of the FIRs lodged under Section
379 and 411 of IPC, a compromise has been entered
into between the parties and the matter was disposed of
in terms of compromise dated 19.07.2024 before
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Muzaffarnagar,
while the second FIR is still pending. The case
registered on the basis of the second FIR under Section
323, 504 and 506 IPC is still pending at trial stage.
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that the disposal of the criminal case on the basis of
the compounding application is an acquittal in view of
the provision to Section 320 Sub section 8 of the
Cr.P.C. and insofar as the other case is concerned, that
is still pending, which does not come within the
category of an offence of moral turpitude, and therefore
only on account of lodging of the two FIRs against the
petitioner, the petitioner cannot be deprived of
appointment by the respondents. He, therefore, filed
writ petitions challenging the illegal and arbitrary
action of the respondents.
4

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
13. Learned counsel for the respondent-State
submits that the State has filed counter-affidavit in
both these two writ petitions.
14. The State has annexed the Service Rules
known as The Uttaranchal Sarkari Vibhag Driver Seva
Niyamawali 2003 and on the basis of Rule 13 of the
aforesaid Rules, it is stated and argued that for the
purpose of service, the character of the candidate should
be such that he should be found suitable in every respect
for employment and the appointing authority itself
satisfies it in respect of the character of the candidate.
15. Since there were two FIRs lodged against the
petitioner and as per the LIU report as well as police
report, the character of the petitioner was not found up
to the mark, the appointing authority has arrived to the
conclusion that the character of the petitioner is not such
to give him appointment. It is also contended by the
learned Standing Counsel that up to the level of
document verification, the petitioner has got full
opportunity to disclose the pendency of lodging of the two
FIRs against him.
16. In the connected writ petition, i.e. WPSS No.
60 of 2025, the counter affidavit has been filed by the
State taking the same stand and justifying the rejection
of the representation of the petitioner vide impugned
order dated 03.01.2025. The petitioner has filed the
rejoinder affidavit reiterating the facts mentioned in the
writ petition and it has been stated that mere pendency
of a criminal case at trial stage cannot bar the petitioner
for appointment.
17. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record of the writ petition.
5

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
18. The facts, as reflected from the perusal of the
record can be called out that two FIRs, i.e. FIR No. 0055
of 2023 dated 02.03.2023 and FIR No. 0316 of 2023,
dated 09.12.2023, have been lodged against the
petitioner. It is admitted fact that both these FIRs were
lodged against the petitioner after the submission of the
application by the petitioner on 11.09.2021. It is also an
admitted fact that in one of the FIRs, the offence has
been compounded by the petitioner vide compromise
dated 19.07.2024 and the Criminal Case No.55 of 2023,
pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Muzzafarnagar, has been decided and the
petitioner has been acquitted by the learned trial court
vide order dated 19.07.2024. The other criminal case
under Section 323, 504, 506 IPC is still pending before
the learned trial court.
19. The perusal of the impugned order dated
03.01.2025, (impugned in WPSS No. 60 of 2025 Vijay
Kumar vs. State of Uttarakhand and others) reveals that
the petitioner has been denied appointment for the
suppression of the information and second on the basis
of the report submitted by the LIU regarding the
character of the petitioner.
20. Insofar as the suppression part is concerned,
there is no suppression of fact of lodging of FIRs against
the petitioner, as both the FIRs were subsequent to the
filing of the application by the petitioner dated
11.09.2021. The report of the LIU and the police is only
with regard to the pendency of FIRs against the petitioner
and, therefore, it has been stated that the character of
the petitioner is not up to the mark and he cannot be
given appointment. If we read Rule 13 of the Uttaranchal
6

UKHC010004792025
2026:UHC:8522
Sarkari Vibhag Driver Seva Niyamawali 2003, the
satisfaction has to be recorded by the appointing
authority on the basis of the material supplied with, the
LIU and police has the right only to send report to the
appointing authority but in the case in hand the police
and LIU has expressed an opinion regarding the
character of the petitioner. The satisfaction has to be
recorded by the appointing authority. In the impugned
order dated 03.01.2025, it has been stated that the due
to the negative report submitted by the police and the
LIU, offering appointment to the petitioner would not be
justifiable.
21. This Court is of the view that such an opinion
cannot be given by the appointing authority. Moreover,
the mere pendency of the case against the petitioner
cannot deprive him of the appointment on the post of
driver. The case filed under Section 323, 504 and 506 of
IPC is pending as yet at the trial stage and the petitioner
has not been convicted, while the other criminal case has
already been compounded and the petitioner has been
acquitted.
22. In such view of the matter, both the writ
petitions stand allowed. The impugned order dated
03.01.2025 passed by respondent No.2 is quashed and
the respondents are directed to issue appointment
letter to the petitioner within a period of one month
from today.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
22.09.2026
Nahid/R.Bisht
7
